t: A civilisation of Peru’s north coast, c. 100–800 CE, whose lords ruled irrigated desert valleys from huge adobe platforms such as the Huaca del Sol.
Its potters made lifelike portrait vessels and painted scenes of combat and sacrifice; its smiths plated copper with gold and silver.
Royal tombs at Sipán and El Brujo reveal warrior-priests and powerful women; climate crises and unrest ended it around 800.
dyk: One Moche man, nicknamed ‘Cut Lip’ by the archaeologist Christopher Donnan for the scar on his lip, survives in some forty portrait vessels showing him from boyhood to middle age.
ev: Moche culture emerges in the Moche and Chicama valleys of Peru’s north coast
The Lord of Sipán is buried with gold, silver and copper regalia in the Lambayeque valley
The tattooed Lady of Cao is buried with war clubs at Huaca Cao Viejo in the Chicama valley
A severe drought recorded in Andean ice cores, with El Niño floods, strains Moche agriculture
Late Moche centres grow at Galindo in the Moche valley and at Pampa Grande in Lambayeque
Pampa Grande is burned and abandoned, probably after a revolt
Galindo is abandoned and the Moche tradition comes to an end
Walter Alva excavates the intact tomb of the Lord of Sipán at Huaca Rajada

f.capital: Huacas de Moche; later Galindo and Pampa Grande
